tasks.//typecheck:js: Typechecks the JS/TS the repo owns — the bench harness, scripts/, and the tsv_debug Deno sidecar — which `deno task typecheck` (cargo) does not see. Directory arguments, not per-directory globs: deno walks them (skipping node_modules) so a new subdirectory is covered the day it appears, where a glob list silently is not. The sidecar is a second invocation because it takes neither the harness config nor its node_modules — and it needs `--no-lock`, since it imports npm by specifier and would otherwise MINT a root deno.lock in a repo that is deliberately lock-free (benches/js/deno.json already sets `lock: false` for the first leg). NOT in `deno task check`: the harness imports npm packages by bare specifier, so this needs `deno task bench:install`, and CI's check job deliberately installs no node_modules (.github/workflows/check.yml). Same posture as test:deno:canonical — run it after a harness, scripts, or sidecar change.
tasks.typecheck:js: deno check --config benches/js/deno.json benches/js scripts && deno check --no-lock crates/tsv_debug/src/deno/sidecar.ts

tasks.//rsvelte-allow-run: The rsvelte-fmt row spawns a prebuilt binary (it ships no in-process API — see benches/js/lib/rsvelte.ts), so `bench:deno:run` and `smoke` must permit it by path. All five published platform packages are listed because the task string is static while the installed one is per-machine; Deno ignores a nonexistent path entry silently (unlike a bare NAME, which logs a resolution failure), so the four that don't apply cost nothing. Node and Bun need no equivalent.
